learner_message: quotes make it easy for python, it does not have to look anywhere to find what it means or what its value is? It simply prints/outputs the whatever that exists within those quotes - that is it for python. But when it encounters any unquoted word as the value of a variable, it starts looking for its latest assigned value. it can also be None. It outputs whatever the latest assigned value of the variable is. In case, the variable has no assigned value, python throws the NameError.
active_question: What changes when a word is quoted rather than written as a variable name, and what does reassignment change?
